concerns.text: The power analysis assumes that ≥20 test molecules are sufficient to detect an R² ≥ 0.7 and a 0.05 improvement over baseline. With only 20 points the confidence interval for R² is wide, making the claim in SC‑001 statistically fragile. A more rigorous power calculation (e.g., bootstrap or simulation for the GNN) or a larger test set should be required.

The validation requires ≥12 of the top‑20 substructures to match the curated motif set and an enrichment > 1.5× random baseline, but the plan does not define a statistical significance test (e.g., p‑value) for the enrichment, nor does it control for multiple hypothesis testing. This weakens the inferential validity of the interpretability claim.

concerns.location: plan.md:Interpretability (FR‑012 handling of unseen atom/bond types)
concerns.text: Molecules containing atom or bond types unseen during training are simply skipped during evaluation. This selective exclusion can bias performance metrics if such molecules are systematically harder to predict, potentially inflating reported R² and undermining the fairness of the comparison.

The plan allows either Integrated Gradients or SHAP but does not specify which will be used, nor does it provide a validation of the chosen attribution method’s reliability for graph neural networks. Different methods can yield divergent substructure rankings, threatening construct validity of the reported top‑20 substructures.

The reference motif set is pruned by removing any motif that appears in the training or test splits. This removal may drastically shrink the reference set, making the ≥60 % overlap criterion easier to satisfy and potentially inflating the apparent enrichment. The plan should ensure the reference set remains sufficiently comprehensive after pruning.
